questions.q: A pyramid has an equilateral triangle as its base, of which each side is 8 cm. Its slant edge is 24 cm. The whole surface area of the pyramid (in cm²) is:
options: (16sqrt3+2435​)
(12sqrt3+2435​)
(24sqrt3+3635​)
(16sqrt3+4835​)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Base Area (Equilateral) = (√3/4) × 8² = 16√3 cm².

Slant height (l) of a face = √(Slant edge² − (Side/2)²) = √(24² − 4²) = 4√35 cm.

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 3 × (1/2 × 8 × 4√35) = 48√35 cm².

Whole Surface Area = Base Area + LSA = (16√3 + 48√35) cm².

∴ The correct answer is (16√3 + 48√35) cm².

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of equilateral base (a) = 8 cm

Slant edge (e) = 24 cm

Formula Used:

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × side²

Slant height (l) = √(slant edge² − (side/2)²)

Whole Surface Area (WSA) = Base Area + 3 × (Lateral Face Area)



⇒ Area of base = (√3 / 4) × 8 × 8 = 16√3 cm²

⇒ Half of base side = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm

⇒ Slant height (l) = √(24² − 4²) = √(576 − 16) = √560

⇒ l = √(16 × 35) = 4√35 cm

⇒ Area of one lateral face = 1/2 × base × l = 1/2 × 8 × 4√35 = 16√35 cm²

⇒ Total Lateral Surface Area = 3 × 16√35 = 48√35 cm²

⇒ Whole Surface Area = Base Area + LSA = (16√3 + 48√35) cm²

∴ The correct answer is (16√3 + 48√35) cm².

Additional Information

Volume of a Pyramid

The volume of any pyramid is given by V = (1/3) × Base Area × Vertical Height (h).

Slant Height vs Vertical Height

For a regular pyramid, l² = h² + r², where l is the slant height, h is the vertical height, and r is the inradius of the base.

Regular Tetrahedron

A regular tetrahedron is a special pyramid where all four faces are congruent equilateral triangles; its total surface area is √3 × a².

questions.q: If the highest common factor (HCF) of x and y is 15, then the HCF of 36x² - 81y² and 81x² - 9y² is divisible by .
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let x = 15 and y = 15 as HCF(15, 15) = 15.

First term: 36(15²) − 81(15²) = 225 × (36 − 81) = 225 × (−45)

Second term: 81(15²) − 9(15²) = 225 × (81 − 9) = 225 × 72

HCF of terms = 225 × HCF(45, 72) = 225 × 9 = 2025.

Among options, 2025 ÷ 135 = 15 (Perfectly divisible).

∴ The correct answer is 135.

Alternate Method

Given: HCF(x, y) = 15

Formula: If HCF(x, y) = h, then x = ha and y = hb, where HCF(a, b) = 1.



⇒ Let x = 15a and y = 15b.

⇒ 36x² − 81y² = 36(15a)² − 81(15b)²

⇒ 36(225a²) − 81(225b²) = 225(36a² − 81b²) = 225 × 9(4a² − 9b²) = 2025(4a² − 9b²)

⇒ 81x² − 9y² = 81(15a)² − 9(15b)²

⇒ 81(225a²) − 9(225b²) = 225(81a² − 9b²) = 225 × 9(9a² − b²) = 2025(9a² − b²)

⇒ The HCF of the two expressions is a multiple of 2025.

⇒ We need to find which option divides 2025.

⇒ 2025 ÷ 135 = 15

⇒ 2025 ÷ 120 = 16.875

⇒ 2025 ÷ 180 = 11.25

⇒ 2025 ÷ 90 = 22.5

∴ The correct answer is 135.

Additional Information

HCF Scaling Property

If HCF(x, y) = k, then HCF(xⁿ, yⁿ) = kⁿ. Similarly, HCF(cx, cy) = c × HCF(x, y).

Algebraic Divisibility

For any expressions f(x, y) and g(x, y), their HCF will always be divisible by the HCF of the common numerical coefficients and the HCF of the base variables.

Divisibility Rule of 135

A number is divisible by 135 if it is divisible by both 5 and 27 (where 27 requires the sum of digits to be a multiple of 9 and satisfying higher power checks).

questions.q: What is the perimeter of a square inscribed in a circle of radius 5 cm?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Diagonal of an inscribed square = Diameter of the circle.

Diameter = 2 × Radius = 2 × 5 = 10 cm.

Perimeter of square = 2√2 × Diagonal.

Perimeter = 2√2 × 10 = 20√2 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 20√2 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the circle (r) = 5 cm

Formula Used:

Diameter of circle (d) = 2 × r

Diagonal of square (D) = Side × √2

Perimeter of square = 4 × Side



Calculations:

⇒ Diameter of the circle = 2 × 5 = 10 cm

⇒ Since the square is inscribed, its diagonal (D) = Diameter of the circle = 10 cm

⇒ Side × √2 = 10

⇒ Side = 10 ÷ √2 = 5√2 cm

⇒ Perimeter of square = 4 × 5√2

⇒ Perimeter = 20√2 cm

∴ The correct answer is 20√2 cm.

Additional Information

Area of Inscribed Square

The area of a square inscribed in a circle of radius r is given by 2r².

Square Circumscribing a Circle

If a square circumscribes a circle, its side is equal to the diameter (2r) and its perimeter is 8r.

Diagonal Property

The diagonal of a square with side 'a' is a√2, and it is the longest distance between any two points in the square.

questions.q: If the curved surface area of a cylinder is 126 π cm² and its height is 14 cm, what is the volume of the cylinder?
options: 28321​ π cm³
13721​ π cm3
12821​ π cm3
12521​ π cm3
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius (r) = Curved Surface Area ÷ (2 × π × height)

r = 126π ÷ (2 × π × 14) = 126 ÷ 28 = 4.5 cm

Volume of cylinder = Curved Surface Area × (r ÷ 2)

Volume = 126π × (4.5 ÷ 2) = 126π × 2.25 = 283.5π cm³

∴ The correct answer is 283½ π cm³.

Alternate Method

Given:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 126π cm²

Height (h) = 14 cm

Formula Used:

CSA of cylinder = 2πrh

Volume of cylinder = πr²h



Calculations:

⇒ 2 × π × r × 14 = 126 × π

⇒ 28 × r = 126

⇒ r = 126 ÷ 28 = 4.5 cm

⇒ Volume = π × (4.5)² × 14

⇒ Volume = π × 20.25 × 14

⇒ Volume = 283.5π cm³

⇒ Volume = 283½ π cm³

∴ The correct answer is 283½ π cm³.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder has exactly one-third of its volume: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Relation between Volume and CSA

For any cylinder, the ratio of its volume to its curved surface area is always r/2, simplified as V = CSA × (r/2).

questions.q: A, B, and C invested capital in the ratio of 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 8. At the end of the business term, they received the profit in the ratio of 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5. What is the ratio of their invested time?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In partnership: Profit = Capital × Time ⇒ Time = Profit ÷ Capital.

Time ratio = (2 ÷ 3) : (3 ÷ 4) : (5 ÷ 8).

LCM of denominators (3, 4, 8) = 24.

Multiply each part by 24: (2/3 × 24) : (3/4 × 24) : (5/8 × 24).

Time ratio = 16 : 18 : 15.

∴ The correct answer is 16 : 18 : 15.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of Capitals (CA : CB : CC) = 3 : 4 : 8

Ratio of Profits (PA : PB : PC) = 2 : 3 : 5

Formula Used:

Profit = Capital × Investment Time

Time = Profit ÷ Capital



Calculations:

⇒ Time of A (TA) = PA ÷ CA = 2 ÷ 3

⇒ Time of B (TB) = PB ÷ CB = 3 ÷ 4

⇒ Time of C (TC) = PC ÷ CC = 5 ÷ 8

⇒ TA : TB : TC = (2/3) : (3/4) : (5/8)

⇒ To simplify, multiply by LCM(3, 4, 8) = 24

⇒ TA = 2/3 × 24 = 16

⇒ TB = 3/4 × 24 = 18

⇒ TC = 5/8 × 24 = 15

⇒ Ratio = 16 : 18 : 15

∴ The correct answer is 16 : 18 : 15.

Additional Information

Capital Calculation

If profit ratio and time ratio are given, the ratio of capital can be found as Capital = Profit ÷ Time.

Active vs Sleeping Partner

An active partner manages the business and may receive a fixed percentage of total profit as salary before the remaining profit is distributed.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest different amounts for different periods of time, the profit is shared according to the ratio of their (Capital × Time) products.

questions.q: The probabilities of solving a problem by three students A, B and C are 73​,95​ and 51​ respectively. The probability that problem will be solved is:
options: 315155​
31564​
315251​
31532​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Probability (Solved) = 1 − Probability (None solve it)

Failure rates: A = 4/7, B = 4/9, C = 4/5

P(None solve) = 4/7 × 4/9 × 4/5 = 64/315

P(Solved) = 1 − 64/315 = 251/315

∴ The correct answer is 251/315.

Alternate Method

Given:

P(A) = 3/7, P(B) = 5/9, P(C) = 1/5

Formula Used:

Probability that the problem is solved = 1 − P(A') × P(B') × P(C')



Calculations:

⇒ P(A') = 1 − 3/7 = 4/7

⇒ P(B') = 1 − 5/9 = 4/9

⇒ P(C') = 1 − 1/5 = 4/5

⇒ Probability that none of them solve the problem = P(A') × P(B') × P(C')

⇒ P(none) = (4/7) × (4/9) × (4/5)

⇒ P(none) = 64 / 315

⇒ Probability that the problem is solved = 1 − P(none)

⇒ P(solved) = 1 − 64/315

⇒ P(solved) = (315 − 64) / 315 = 251 / 315

∴ The correct answer is 251/315.

Additional Information

Independent Events

Two events are independent if the occurrence of one does not affect the other. For such events, P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).

At Least One Event

The probability of at least one event occurring among independent events is calculated as 1 − P(none of the events occur).

Complementary Probability

The sum of the probability of an event and its complement is always 1: P(E) + P(E') = 1.

questions.q: Reshma covers 45 km at a speed of 15 km/h by bicycle, 80 km at a speed of 40 km/h by car, and another 6 km at a speed of 2 km/h on foot. Find her average speed for the whole journey (correct to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Distance = 45 + 80 + 6 = 131 km

Total Time = (45 ÷ 15) + (80 ÷ 40) + (6 ÷ 2) = 3 + 2 + 3 = 8 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 131 ÷ 8 = 16.375 km/h

Rounding to 2 decimal places ≈ 16.38 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 16.38 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance₁ (d₁) = 45 km, Speed₁ (s₁) = 15 km/h

Distance₂ (d₂) = 80 km, Speed₂ (s₂) = 40 km/h

Distance₃ (d₃) = 6 km, Speed₃ (s₃) = 2 km/h

Formula Used:

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed



Calculations:

⇒ Total Distance = d₁ + d₂ + d₃

⇒ Total Distance = 45 + 80 + 6 = 131 km

⇒ Time t₁ = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours

⇒ Time t₂ = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours

⇒ Time t₃ = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 hours

⇒ Total Time = t₁ + t₂ + t₃ = 3 + 2 + 3 = 8 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 131 ÷ 8

⇒ Average Speed = 16.375 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 16.38 km/h.

Additional Information

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

If a journey is divided into two equal parts with speeds x and y, then Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Average Speed General Case

Average speed is always the total displacement (or total distance for scalar cases) divided by the total time taken, regardless of intermediate stops.

questions.q: A dishonest dealer marks up his goods by 50% and then gives a discount of 20% on the marked price. Apart from this, he uses a faulty balance which reads 1kg for 900 gm. What is his net profit percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net Multiplier = (Markup Factor) × (Discount Factor) × (Weight Factor)

Markup 50% → 3/2 | Discount 20% → 4/5 | Faulty weight (reads 1000 for 900) → 10/9

Net Ratio = (3/2) × (4/5) × (10/9) = (120 / 90) = 4/3

Profit % = (4 − 3)/3 × 100 = 33.33% ≈ 33%

∴ The correct answer is 33%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Markup % = 50%

Discount % = 20%

Faulty Balance = 1 kg (1000 gm) instead of 900 gm



Let the CP of 1000 gm be ₹1000.

⇒ CP of 900 gm = ₹900 (This is the dealer's actual cost for what he gives).

⇒ Marked Price (MP) for 1000 gm = ₹1000 + 50% of 1000 = ₹1500.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) after 20% discount on MP = ₹1500 − 20% of 1500

⇒ SP = ₹1500 − ₹300 = ₹1200.

⇒ The dealer gives only 900 gm but charges for 1000 gm at SP.

⇒ Profit = SP − Actual CP of 900 gm = ₹1200 − ₹900 = ₹300.

⇒ Profit % = (Profit / Actual CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (300 / 900) × 100 = 1/3 × 100 = 33.33%

⇒ Rounded to nearest integer = 33%.

∴ The correct answer is 33%.

Additional Information

Dishonest Dealer Formula

Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) / False Weight] × 100. This is the profit due to weight manipulation only.

Successive Percentage Rule

When two changes x% and y% are applied, net change = [x + y + (xy/100)]%. For markup (positive) and discount (negative), x = markup and y = −discount.

Combined Effective Profit

Net SP/CP Ratio = (1 + markup/100) × (1 − discount/100) × (True Weight / False Weight). Profit % = (Ratio − 1) × 100.

questions.q: If △ABC is right angled at B, AB = 12 cm and ∠CAB = 60°, determine the length of BC.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a right-angled triangle with angles 30°, 60°, and 90°, the ratio of sides opposite to these angles is 1 : √3 : 2.

Here, ∠B = 90°, ∠A = 60°, therefore ∠C = 30°.

The side AB is opposite to ∠C (30°), so AB = 1 unit = 12 cm.

The side BC is opposite to ∠A (60°), so BC = √3 units = 12 × √3 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 12√3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Triangle ABC is right-angled at B (∠ABC = 90°).

Length of AB = 12 cm.

Angle ∠CAB = 60°.

Formula Used:

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = (Side Opposite to θ) ÷ (Side Adjacent to θ)



Calculations:

In ΔABC, for angle A = 60°:

⇒ tan(∠CAB) = BC ÷ AB

⇒ tan 60° = BC ÷ 12

⇒ √3 = BC ÷ 12

⇒ BC = 12 × √3

⇒ BC = 12√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 12√3 cm.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios

For any angle θ, sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, and tan θ = Opp/Adj.

Special Values

Common values include tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right triangle, Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular² (AC² = AB² + BC²).

Sum of Angles

The interior angles of any triangle always add up to 180° (∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°).

questions.q: Find the number of diagonals of a regular polygon, sum of whose interior angles is 2700°
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Number of sides (n) = (Sum of interior angles ÷ 180) + 2

n = (2700 ÷ 180) + 2 = 15 + 2 = 17

Number of diagonals = n × (n − 3) ÷ 2

Number of diagonals = 17 × 14 ÷ 2 = 119

∴ The correct answer is 119.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sum of interior angles = 2700°

Formula Used:

1. Sum of interior angles of a polygon = (n − 2) × 180°

2. Number of diagonals = [n × (n − 3)] ÷ 2

where n = number of sides.



Calculations:

⇒ (n − 2) × 180° = 2700°

⇒ n − 2 = 2700 ÷ 180

⇒ n − 2 = 15

⇒ n = 15 + 2 = 17

⇒ Number of diagonals = [17 × (17 − 3)] ÷ 2

⇒ Number of diagonals = (17 × 14) ÷ 2

⇒ Number of diagonals = 17 × 7 = 119

∴ The correct answer is 119.

Additional Information

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any convex polygon, the sum of all exterior angles is always 360°.

Interior and Exterior Angle Relation

At each vertex of a regular polygon, Interior Angle + Exterior Angle = 180°.

Each Interior Angle of Regular Polygon

The measure of each interior angle is calculated as [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n.

Each Exterior Angle of Regular Polygon

The measure of each exterior angle is calculated as 360° ÷ n.

questions.q: In 5 years, the simple interest on an amount of Rs. X is 52​th of the principal. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest = 2/5 of Principal = (2/5 × 100)% = 40% of Principal.

Total Interest % = Rate × Time

40% = Rate × 5 years

Rate = 40% ÷ 5 = 8%

∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = Rs. X

Time (T) = 5 years

Simple Interest (SI) = 2/5 of X = 0.4X

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100



Calculations:

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ (2/5) × X = (X × R × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ 2/5 = 5R ÷ 100

⇒ 0.4 = R ÷ 20

⇒ R = 0.4 × 20

⇒ R = 8%

∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Components

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100. If any three variables are known, the fourth can be calculated directly.

Effective Rate of Interest

The total percentage change in the principal over T years at R% simple interest per year is (R × T)%.

Total Amount Formula

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI) = P × (1 + RT/100).

questions.q: The difference between the length of two parallel sides of a trapezium is 12 cm. The perpendicular distance between these two parallel sides is 60 cm. If the area of the trapezium is 1380 cm², then find the length of each of the parallel sides (in cm).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of parallel sides = (2 × Area) ÷ Height

⇒ Sum = (2 × 1380) ÷ 60 = 46 cm.

Given Difference = 12 cm.

Sides = (Sum ± Difference) ÷ 2 = (46 ± 12) ÷ 2 = 29 cm and 17 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 29, 17 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Area of trapezium = 1380 cm²

Height (h) = 60 cm

Difference between parallel sides (a − b) = 12 cm

Formula used: Area of trapezium = 1/2 × (a + b) × h



⇒ 1380 = 1/2 × (a + b) × 60

⇒ 1380 = 30 × (a + b)

⇒ a + b = 1380 ÷ 30

⇒ a + b = 46 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ a − b = 12 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding (1) and (2): 2a = 58 ⇒ a = 29 cm

⇒ Substituting in (1): 29 + b = 46 ⇒ b = 17 cm

∴ The correct answer is 29, 17 cm.

Additional Information

Area of Trapezium

The area is calculated as the product of the average of the parallel sides and the perpendicular distance between them: Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height.

Median of a Trapezium

The median (mid-segment) is parallel to the bases and its length is the average of the bases: Median = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Isosceles Trapezium

A trapezium where the non-parallel sides are equal in length and the base angles are also equal.

questions.q: For a sample data, mean = 60 and median = 48. For this distribution, the mode is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct Empirical Formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

Substitute: Mode = 3(48) − 2(60)

Calculate: 144 − 120 = 24

∴ The correct answer is 24.

Alternate Method

Given:

Mean = 60

Median = 48

Formula Used:

For a moderately skewed distribution, the empirical relation is:

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean



Calculations:

⇒ Mode = 3 × 48 − 2 × 60

⇒ Mode = 144 − 120

⇒ Mode = 24

∴ The correct answer is 24.

Additional Information

Empirical Relation (Karl Pearson)

The relationship Mean − Mode = 3 × (Mean − Median) is used for moderately skewed asymmetrical distributions.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness Identification

When Mean > Median > Mode, the distribution is positively skewed; if Mode > Median > Mean, it is negatively skewed.

questions.q: The centroid of an equilateral triangle PQR is L. If PQ = 6 cm, the length of PL is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In an equilateral triangle, the distance from any vertex to the centroid (L) is equal to its circumradius (R).

Shortcut formula: PL = Side / √3

Given side PQ = 6 cm

PL = 6 / √3 = (2 × 3) / √3 = 2√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of equilateral triangle PQR (a) = 6 cm

L is the centroid of the triangle.

Formula used:

1. Altitude (h) of an equilateral triangle = (√3 / 2) × a

2. Centroid divides the median (altitude in this case) in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex.



Calculations:

⇒ Altitude (PM) = (√3 / 2) × 6

⇒ PM = 3√3 cm

⇒ PL = (2 / 3) × PM

⇒ PL = (2 / 3) × 3√3

⇒ PL = 2√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.

Additional Information

Centroid of a Triangle

The point where all three medians of a triangle intersect. It divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

Equilateral Triangle Properties

For a side length a, the circumradius R = a / √3, and the inradius r = a / (2√3). The centroid, orthocenter, circumcenter, and incenter all coincide at the same point.

Area and Height

Height h = (√3 / 2) × a and Area = (√3 / 4) × a².

questions.q: Find the exact value of cos 120°.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

120° lies in the Second Quadrant (90° to 180°).

In the Second Quadrant, the Cosine function is always negative.

Reference Angle = 180° − 120° = 60°.

cos 120° = −cos 60° = −0.5.

∴ The correct answer is −0.5.

Alternate Method

Given: Angle = 120°

Formula Used: cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ



⇒ cos 120° can be written as cos(180° − 60°).

⇒ We know that cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ.

⇒ cos 120° = −cos 60°.

⇒ Since cos 60° = 0.5 (or 1/2).

⇒ cos 120° = −0.5.

∴ The correct answer is −0.5.

Additional Information

ASTC Rule (Quadrant System)

All (Q-I), Silver (Q-II: Sin/Cosec), Tea (Q-III: Tan/Cot), Cups (Q-IV: Cos/Sec) identifies where functions are positive.

Standard Cosine Values

cos 0° = 1, cos 30° = √3/2, cos 45° = 1/√2, cos 60° = 0.5, cos 90° = 0.

Angle Reduction Formulas

cos(90° + θ) = −sin θ | cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ | cos(180° + θ) = −cos θ | cos(360° − θ) = cos θ.

questions.q: If 4x² + y² = 40 and xy = 6, then find the value of 2x + y.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Note the identity: (2x + y)² = 4x² + y² + 4xy.

Substitute the known values 4x² + y² = 40 and xy = 6.

(2x + y)² = 40 + 4 × 6 = 40 + 24 = 64.

Taking the square root on both sides: 2x + y = √64 = 8.

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method

Given:

4x² + y² = 40

xy = 6

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

Calculations:

⇒ Consider the expression (2x + y)².

⇒ By applying the algebraic identity, (2x + y)² = (2x)² + (y)² + 2 × (2x) × (y)

⇒ (2x + y)² = 4x² + y² + 4xy

⇒ Substituting the given values: (2x + y)² = 40 + 4 × 6

⇒ (2x + y)² = 40 + 24

⇒ (2x + y)² = 64

⇒ 2x + y = √64

⇒ 2x + y = 8

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Additional Information

Square of a Binomial Sum

The identity (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² is used to relate the sum of squares and the product of two terms to the square of their sum.

Square of a Binomial Difference

Difference of Two Squares

The identity a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) is essential for factorising expressions involving the subtraction of two perfect squares.

questions.q: The ratio of the number of coins of 25 paise, 50 paise, Rs. 2 and Rs. 5 is 5 ∶ 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 1, respectively. If the total amount of the coins is Rs. 285, then the difference between the number of 25 paise and Rs. 5 coins is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Value ratio = (5 × 0.25) : (4 × 0.50) : (3 × 2) : (1 × 5) = 1.25 : 2 : 6 : 5

Sum of ratio parts = 1.25 + 2 + 6 + 5 = 14.25

Value of 1 unit = 285 ÷ 14.25 = 20

Difference in count between 25 paise and ₹5 coins = (5 − 1) × 20 = 4 × 20 = 80

∴ The correct answer is 80 coins.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of number of coins (25p : 50p : ₹2 : ₹5) = 5 : 4 : 3 : 1

Total amount = ₹285

Formula Used:

Total Value = ∑ (Denomination × Number of coins)



Let the number of coins be 5x, 4x, 3x, and 1x.

Total value in ₹ = (Number of 25p coins × 0.25) + (Number of 50p coins × 0.50) + (Number of ₹2 coins × 2) + (Number of ₹5 coins × 5)

⇒ (5x × 0.25) + (4x × 0.50) + (3x × 2) + (1x × 5) = 285

⇒ 1.25x + 2x + 6x + 5x = 285

⇒ 14.25x = 285

⇒ x = 285 ÷ 14.25

⇒ x = 20

Number of 25 paise coins = 5x = 5 × 20 = 100

Number of ₹5 coins = 1x = 1 × 20 = 20

Difference = 100 − 20 = 80

∴ The correct answer is 80 coins.

Additional Information

Unit Conversion

Always ensure all denominations are in the same unit (either all in paise or all in rupees) before calculation. 1 Rupee = 100 Paise.

Value vs Count Ratio

If the ratio of values is given as V₁ : V₂, the ratio of the number of coins is (V₁/D₁) : (V₂/D₂), where D is the denomination.

Combined Ratio

For three or more items, the total amount is ∑(Ratio Part × Denomination) × Constant = Total Money.

If every observation in a set is increased or decreased by a constant value 'k', the average also increases or decreases by 'k'.

questions.q: For what value of m will the system of equations 18x - 72y + 13 = 0 and 7x - my - 17 = 0 have no solution?
questions.solution:

For a system of equations to have no solution, the lines must be parallel, where the ratio of x and y coefficients are equal.

Ratio of x-coefficients: 18 ÷ 7

Ratio of y-coefficients: −72 ÷ (−m) = 72/m

Equating ratios: 18/7 = 72/m

m = (72 × 7) ÷ 18 ⇒ 4 × 7 = 28

∴ The correct answer is 28.

Given equations: 18x − 72y + 13 = 0 and 7x − my − 17 = 0.

Comparing with the standard form a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0:

a₁ = 18, b₁ = −72, c₁ = 13

a₂ = 7, b₂ = −m, c₂ = −17

⇒ 18/7 = 72/m

⇒ 18 × m = 72 × 7

⇒ m = (72 × 7) ÷ 18

⇒ m = 4 × 7

⇒ m = 28

Check: 18/7 ≠ 13/−17, which holds true.

∴ The correct answer is 28.

A system of linear equations has a unique solution if the lines intersect: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂.

Infinite Solutions

A system has infinite solutions if the lines are coincident: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

Consistency

A system is consistent if it has at least one solution (unique or infinite) and inconsistent if it has no solution.

questions.q: The number 1254216 is divisible by which of the following numbers?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To check divisibility by 8, only the last three digits of the number need to be checked.

The last three digits of 1254216 are 216.

216 ÷ 8 = 27

Since 216 is perfectly divisible by 8, the entire number 1254216 is divisible by 8.

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method

Given: Number = 1254216

Formula/Rules Used:

1. Divisibility by 5: Last digit must be 0 or 5.

2. Divisibility by 11: (Sum of digits at odd places) − (Sum of digits at even places) must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

3. Divisibility by 16: Last four digits must be divisible by 16.

4. Divisibility by 8: Last three digits must be divisible by 8.

Calculations:

⇒ Check for 5: Last digit is 6. Not divisible by 5.

⇒ Check for 11: (6 + 2 + 5 + 1) − (1 + 4 + 2) = 14 − 7 = 7. Not divisible by 11.

⇒ Check for 16: Last four digits are 4216. 4216 ÷ 16 = 263.5. Not divisible by 16.

⇒ Check for 8: Last three digits are 216. 216 ÷ 8 = 27. Divisible by 8.

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Additional Information

Divisibility by powers of 2

A number is divisible by 2ⁿ if its last n digits are divisible by 2ⁿ. For 2 (2¹), check last 1 digit; for 4 (2²), check last 2 digits; for 8 (2³), check last 3 digits.

Divisibility by 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 or 9, respectively.

Divisibility by 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is simultaneously divisible by both 2 (even number) and 3 (sum of digits divisible by 3).

‘A # B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’.

If D @ N @ H & Y @ F % V, then how is Y related to D?
questions.solution:
Method:
1. Decode the symbols: @ means daughter, & means husband, % means wife.
2. Break the expression: D @ N (D is daughter of N) → N @ H (N is daughter of H) → H & Y (H is husband of Y) → Y @ F (Y is daughter of F) → F % V (F is wife of V).
3. Trace the lineage: H is the husband of Y. Since H is the husband, Y is the wife of H.
4. Connect to D: D is the daughter of N, and N is the daughter of H. Therefore, H is the grandfather of D.
5. Find Y's relation: Since Y is the wife of H (D's grandfather), Y is the grandmother of D.
6. Re-evaluate the path: Wait, let's re-read the chain: D @ N (D is daughter of N), N @ H (N is daughter of H), H & Y (H is husband of Y). This means H and Y are the parents of N.
7. Since N is the mother of D, and Y is the mother of N, Y is the mother's mother (maternal grandmother) of D.

Explanation:
In blood relation problems, always decode the symbols step-by-step to build a family tree. Identify the gender of each person and their generation gap to find the correct relation.

Why the others are wrong:
(A) Mother: Y is one generation above D's mother.
(B) Husband's mother: Y is the mother of D's mother, not the mother of D's husband.
(C) Father's sister: Y is a female in a higher generation.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is The publishers will release a new book on games next week.

Key Points

• The above-given sentence is in the passive voice.

• We need to change it into active voice.

• The following steps need to be taken for converting the sentence into passive voice:-

• The subject 'A new book on games​' of the passive voice will become the object of the active voice.

• The object 'The publishers' of the passive voice will become the subject of the active voice.

• Since modal verb has been used in the active voice, therefore, the passive voice will follow the given structure:-

• Passive Voice - Object + modal verb*(will)* + be + V3 + Subject.

• Active Voice - Subject + modal verb*(will) *+ V1 + Object.

Therefore, the correct passive voice is *The publishers will release a new book on games next week. *

Additional Information

• When we convert active voice to passive voice, three things need to be kept in mind:-

• Change object into subject.

• Change subject into object.

• Always use the third form of the verb in the passive voice.

questions.q: Article 148 of the Constitution of India provides for an independent office of the comptroller and auditor general of india.

questions.q:
Following statements are made regarding global warming.

A. Global warming is the long-term heating of Earth's surface observed since the preindustrial period due to human activities, primarily fossil fuel burning, which increases heat-trapping greenhouse gas levels in Earth's atmosphere.

B. Global warming causes climate change, which poses a serious threat to life on Earth in the forms of widespread flooding and extreme weather.

Which of these statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both A & B.

Key Points

• Global warming

• Global warming refers to the long-term trend of rising temperatures on Earth's surface, which has been observed since the preindustrial period.

• The Earth's temperature is regulated by a balance between incoming solar radiation and outgoing radiation reflected back into space.

• Greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide, trap some of the outgoing radiation, which keeps the Earth's surface warmer than it would otherwise be.

• The Industrial Revolution, which began in the mid-18th century, marked the start of significant human-caused emissions of greenhouse gases.

• Since then, the use of fossil fuels for energy, transportation, and industrial purposes has grown rapidly, leading to an unprecedented increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide levels.

• Multiple lines of evidence, including temperature records, ice core data, and ocean temperature measurements, all support the conclusion that the Earth is warming due to human activities.

• The consequences of global warming are vast and potentially catastrophic.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct about uniform acceleration?
options: An object moving on friction-less surface can gain uniform acceleration

questions.solution:
The correct answer is An object under free fall is an example of uniform acceleration. Key Points

• Uniform acceleration

• Uniform acceleration refers to the motion of an object where the acceleration is constant, meaning the object's velocity changes by the same amount in each unit of time.

• The equations of motion for uniformly accelerated motion are as follows:

• v = u + at (final velocity = initial velocity + acceleration x time)

• s = ut + 1/2at² (displacement = initial velocity x time + 1/2 x acceleration x time²)

• v² = u² + 2as (final velocity² = initial velocity² + 2 x acceleration x displacement)

• where:

• v = final velocity

• u = initial velocity

• a = acceleration

• t = time

• s = displacement

Additional Information

• If any object starts from rest, its initial velocity will be zero.

• In the case of uniform motion, acceleration will be zero.

• For accelerated motion, velocity will vary with time.

• If the velocity of an object is increasing, it represents acceleration.

• If the velocity of an object is decreasing, it will be the case of retardation.

questions.q: How many types of writs can be issued under Article 32 and 226 of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.

Key Points

• Under the Constitution of India, Article 32 provides for the right to constitutional remedies, while Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs. The following are the different types of writs that can be issued under these articles:

• Habeas corpus - to produce a person who is under illegal detention

• Mandamus - to compel a public official or body to perform a duty

• Prohibition - to prohibit a lower court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction

• Certiorari - to quash the order of a lower court or tribunal

• Quo warranto - to question the authority or legality of a person holding a public office

• Thus, a total of five types of writs can be issued under Article 32 and 226 of the Constitution of India.

Additional Information

• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to constitutional remedies to every citizen of India.

• This article empowers the citizens to approach the Supreme Court of India to seek enforcement of their fundamental rights.

• The Supreme Court has the power to issue writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto, for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.

• The right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 is considered as a fundamental right in itself, and any law or action that violates the fundamental rights can be challenged under this article.

• This article ensures that the citizens have a direct access to the Supreme Court, which is the highest court of the land, to seek justice and protection of their rights.

• Article 32 is often regarded as the most important and valuable provision in the Indian Constitution, as it provides a powerful mechanism to protect the fundamental rights of the citizens and to ensure that the government acts in accordance with the Constitution.

• Article 226 of the Constitution of India empowers the High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.

• The High Court, being the highest court in a state, has wide-ranging powers to exercise judicial review over the decisions of inferior courts, tribunals, and other authorities within its territorial jurisdiction.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India introduced a comprehensive regulatory framework for NBFC-MFI on .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.

Key Points

• One key milestone in the evolution of this regulatory framework was the constitution of the committee under the Chairmanship of Shri Y. H. Malegam. Based on the recommendations of this Committee, RBI introduced a comprehensive regulatory framework for NBFC-MFIs in December 2011.

• The regulations prescribed the eligibility criteria for microfinance loans which was linked to core features of microfinance i.e., lending of small amounts to borrowers belonging to low-income groups without collateral, with flexible repayment schedules. Besides, the regulations laid special emphasis on protection of borrowers and fair practices in lending such as transparency in charges, ceilings on margins and interest rates, non-coercive methods of recovery, measures to contain multiple lending and over-indebtedness.

​ Additional Information

• Indian microfinance sector has witnessed phenomenal growth over past two decades in terms of increase in both – the number of institutions providing micro finance as also the quantum of credit made available to the micro finance customers.

• Presently, micro credit is delivered through a variety of institutional channels viz., scheduled commercial banks (SCBs), regional rural banks (RRBs), cooperative banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), Section 8 companies and microfinance institutions (MFIs) registered as NBFCs as well as in other forms. The small finance banks (SFBs) are the latest game in the town.

• The institutional landscape of the microfinance sector has also changed significantly after licensing of Small Finance Banks. One out of two entities which was granted approval for starting a universal bank in 2014 was an NBFC-MFI, while eight out of ten entities granted approval for starting Small Finance Banks in 2016 were NBFC-MFIs.

• This, apart from further consolidation in the sector, has led to significant changes in the market dynamics with the share of specialized MFIs standing at a little over 30 per cent as on June 30, 2021 in the overall gross loan portfolio of around ₹2.14 lakh crore in the sector. Thus, micro finance, as a financial activity can no longer said to be a bastion of specialized MFIs.

• However, the current regulatory framework, which was put in place with the objective of making credit available to low-income households and to protect borrowers from harsh recovery practices of the lenders, is applicable only to NBFC-MFIs, whereas other lenders, who now have a share of around 70 per cent in the microfinance portfolio are not subjected to similar regulatory conditions.

• This has created a non-level playing field, posing difficulties for customers and has resulted in emergence of differing practices within the sector. While one would have expected

• that other lenders would also be guided by the intent of the abovementioned regulations applicable to NBFC- MFIs, that has not happened.

• Mostly, there have been three distinct sets of criticisms against micro finance lenders –

• They lead their borrowers into debt-trap like situations

• They charge usurious rates of interest often disproportionate to their funding and operational costs

• They deploy harsh recovery methods leading to distress amongst borrowers.

• These are issues which need to be critically introspected and addressed by the lenders to prevent recurrence of the crisis episodes. The emerging dynamics in the microfinance sector as well as the concerns around customer protection therefore call for a review of the regulations so that all the regulated entities engaged in micro finance pursue the goal of customer protection within a well-calibrated and harmonized set-up.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Bill, 2022?

A. The Lok Sabha referred this Bill to the joint committee of parliament comprising 21 members from the Lower House and 10 from the Upper House.

B. This Bill also proposed to establish a ‘Cooperative Election Authority’ to bring electoral reforms.

C. The Bill also has a Section — 63A that relates to ‘establishment of the Cooperative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund’ for revival of ‘sick multi-state cooperative societies’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.

Key Points

•

The Bill amends the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002.

•

It establishes the Co-operative Election Authority to conduct and supervise elections to the boards of multi-state co-operative societies. A multi-state co-operative society will require prior permission of government authorities before the redemption of their shareholding.

•

A Co-operative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund will be established for the revival of sick multi-state co-operative societies. The Fund will be financed through contributions by profitable multi-state co-operative societies.

•

The Bill allows state co-operative societies to merge into an existing multi-state co-operative society, subject to the respective state laws.

Additional Information Key Features

• Election of board members:

• Under the Act, elections to the board of a multi-state co-operative society are conducted by its existing board.

• The Bill amends this to specify that the central government will establish the Co-operative Election Authority to:

• conduct such elections,

• supervise, direct, and control the preparation of electoral rolls, and

• perform other prescribed functions.

• The Authority will consist of a chairperson, vice-chairperson, and up to three members appointed by the central government on the recommendations of a selection committee.

• Amalgamation of co-operative societies:

• The Act provides for the amalgamation and division of multi-state co-operative societies.

• This can be done by passing a resolution at a general meeting with at least two-thirds of the members, present and voting.

• The Bill allows state co-operative societies to merge into an existing multi-state co-operative society, subject to the respective state laws.

• At least two-thirds of the members of the co-operative society present and voting at a general meeting must pass a resolution to allow such a merger.

• Fund for sick co-operative societies:

• The Bill establishes the Co-operative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund for revival of sick multi-state co-operative societies. A sick multi-state co-operative society is one that has:

• (i) accumulated losses equal to or exceeding the total of its paid-up capital, free reserves, and surpluses, and

• (ii) suffered cash losses in the past two financial years.

• The central government may prepare a scheme for rehabilitation and reconstruction of the society. Multi-state co-operative societies that are in profit for the preceding three financial years shall finance the Fund.

• They will deposit either one crore rupees or one percent of their net profit into the Fund, whichever is less.

• Restriction on redemption of government shareholding:

• The Act provides that the shares held in a multi-state co-operative society by certain government authorities can be redeemed based on the bye-laws of the society.

• These government authorities include:

• (i) the central government,

• (ii) state governments,

• (iii) the National Co-operative Development Corporation,

• (iv) any corporation owned or controlled by the government, or

• (v) any government company.

• The Bill amends this to provide that any shares held by the central and state governments cannot be redeemed without their prior approval.

• Redressal of complaints:

• ​As per the Bill, the central government will appoint one or more Co-operative Ombudsman with territorial jurisdiction.

• The Ombudsman shall inquire into complaints made by members of multi-state co-operative societies regarding:

• (i) their deposits,

• (ii) equitable benefits of the society’s functioning, or

• (iii) issues affecting the individual rights of the members.

• The Ombudsman shall complete the process of inquiry and adjudication within three months from the receipt of the complaint. Appeals against the directions of the Ombudsman may be filed with the Central Registrar (who is appointed by the central government) within a month.
